fact_en:
What hard mineral forms clear, six-sided crystals on our beaches?

Quartz is a hard, common mineral found in Philippine beaches and rivers! It forms beautiful, clear, six-sided crystal shapes.
fact_bis:
Unsa nga kusog nga mineral ang nagbuhat og klaro nga unom-ka-guyod nga kristal sa mga baybayon?

Ang quartz usa ka kusog, kasagarang mineral nga makita sa mga baybayon ug suba sa Pilipinas! Nagbuhat kini og klaro nga unom-ka-guyod nga kristal.

findings.note: The body's key descriptor is a different word. EN question and answer both say "six-sided crystals"; BIS says "unom-ka-guyod nga kristal" twice — guyod = TO DRAG/PULL everywhere else in this corpus (ffct-24502 'Carry vs Drag', ffct-09052 bottom trawling, ffct-04130 kalesa), so the body reads 'six-drag crystals', which is meaningless. The card's OWN title has the correct word, 'Quartz nga Unom ka Kilid' (kilid = side, 478 corpus uses), which is what makes the body the outlier.

fact_en: Never cross a swollen river during the rainy season because fast-moving flash floods can easily sweep a person off their feet!
fact_bis: Ayaw pagtabok sa nabaha nga suba panahon sa ting-ulan kay ang kusog nga flash flood dali ra kaayo nga makapagligtas sa usa ka tawo!

findings.note: Flash-flood safety card reverses the danger. EN: fast-moving flash floods "can easily sweep a person off their feet". BIS: "ang kusog nga flash flood dali ra kaayo nga makapagligtas sa usa ka tawo" — ligtas/makapagligtas = to save/rescue (corpus uses ligtas only for 'safe': ffct-21197, ffct-24482, ffct-25167). The card now says a strong flash flood can easily SAVE a person, the opposite of the hazard it is warning about; sweep away = makabanlas/makaanod (cf. ffct-32494 'banlasan sa ulan'). Nothing in the card corrects it.

fact_en:
How many earthworms live in healthy agricultural soil?

A single healthy acre can contain more than one million earthworms hiding underground!
fact_bis:
Pila ka earthworms ang nagpuyo sa maayong agrikultural nga yuta?

Sa usa ka ektaryang maayo, mahimong adunay kapin sa usa ka milyon ka earthworms nga nagtago!

findings.note: Unit changed. EN: "A single healthy acre can contain more than one million earthworms". BIS: "Sa usa ka ektaryang maayo" — ektarya is the corpus's word for HECTARE (ffct-38680, ffct-13514, ffct-30170 all render 'hectare' as ektarya), and 1 hectare = 2.47 acres. The Cebuano card states a ~2.5× wrong density and the correct unit appears nowhere on the card.

fact_en:
Why should you drink water during sunny recess?

Drinking water prevents heatstroke because sweating cools your body down through evaporation!
fact_bis:
Nganong mag-inom og tubig sa init nga recess?

Makalikay kini sa heatstroke kay ang pagpanghupaw nag-pa-cool sa lawas pinaagi sa evaporation!

findings.note: The mechanism becomes false. EN: "sweating cools your body down through evaporation". BIS: "ang pagpanghupaw nag-pa-cool sa lawas pinaagi sa evaporation" — panghupaw = SIGHING, not sweating. A child reads that sighing cools the body by evaporation. Cebuano sweat is singot/pagsingot, which this corpus uses 155× (ffct-07477, ffct-13764, ffct-16165). Sweat is never named anywhere on the card, so the fact is unrecoverable.

fact_en: Since the equator crosses the Philippines, places like Basilan get direct, intense sunlight year-round compared to higher latitudes!
fact_bis: Tungod nga moagi ang equator sa Pilipinas, ang mga lugar sama sa Basilan makadawat og direct, intense sunlight sa tibuok tuig!

findings.note: title_bis "Sikad Basilan Tuig" for "Basilan Year-Round Sun". Cebuano sikad = to kick / push off with the foot; it never means sun or sunshine (adlaw / init sa adlaw / sidlak). The title as written is meaningless for the card's subject, and no form of the word appears in the body to correct it. Medium confidence — likely a mangled "sikat" (Tagalog), which is also not Cebuano for sun.

fact_en: Venus is the brightest planet in our solar system! You can easily spot it in the sky just before sunrise or after sunset.
fact_bis: Ang Venus mao ang pinakasilaw nga planeta sa atong solar system! Sayon ra siya makita sa langit sa dili pa mosubang ang adlaw o human mosalop.

findings.note: title_bis "Pinakadasigon: Venus" for "Brightest Planet: Venus". Cebuano dasig = fast/energetic (this same batch uses kadasig for SPEED on the tornado card ffct-35315), never bright. The title therefore asserts a false fact — Venus as the FASTEST planet — and the card's own body uses the correct word ("pinakasilaw nga planeta"), so the title is the outlier.

fact_en:
What gives a typhoon its powerful winds and heavy rain?

Warm tropical ocean water evaporates and rises rapidly, releasing latent heat that fuels the strong, rotating winds and heavy rainfall of a typhoon.
fact_bis:
Unsa ang naghatag sa bagyo og kusog nga hangin ug ulan?

Ang init nga tubig sa tropikal nga dagat mo-evaporate ug paspas nga mosaka, nagpagawas og latent heat nga nagpalig-on sa nag-liko-liko nga hangin ug kusog nga ulan sa bagyo.

findings.note: title_bis "Sungkit sa Bagyo" for "What Fuels a Typhoon". Cebuano sungkit = a pole/hook for picking fruit down; it has no fuel sense (fuel = sugnod). Looks like a corruption of "Sugnod sa Bagyo". The word is never corrected anywhere in the card — the body paraphrases with "nagpalig-on" and keeps the English "latent heat" — so the title names a different thing entirely.

fact_en: Fossils form when organism remains are quickly buried by sediment. Over time, the sediment hardens into rock, preserving its shape or trace!
fact_bis: Maporma ang fossil kung ang salin sa organismo paspas nga matabunan sa sediment. Sa paglabay sa panahon, mahimo kining bato nga magtipig sa porma o timaan!

findings.note: title_bis "Pagbuto Fossil" for "How Fossils Form". Pagbuto in Cebuano = an explosion/eruption (used correctly for eruption in ffct-35409 "Pagbuto sa Bulkan"), not formation. The body uses the right verb ("Maporma ang fossil"), so the title says a different thing: fossils exploding rather than forming.

fact_en: Avoid playing near steep cliffs made of loose shale! Heavy rain can easily trigger dangerous, falling rock fragments.
fact_bis: Likayi ang pagdula duol sa mga matatarik nga bangin nga hinimo sa luag nga shale! Dali ra matumba ang mga bato kung kusog ang ulan.

findings.note: title_bis "Delikado nga Shale Bungbong" for "Dangerous Shale Cliffs". Bungbong in Cebuano = a wall/partition of a house, not a cliff; the body uses the correct word ("matatarik nga bangin"). The title names a different thing (a shale wall) and the safety warning is about cliffs.

fact_en: Heavy rains wash loose volcanic ash down mountains, creating fast, destructive mudflows called lahars!
fact_bis: Gihugasan sa kusog nga ulan ang luag nga abo sa bulkan paingon sa bukid, naghimo og kusog ug makadaut nga alon sa lapok nga gitawag og lahar!

findings.note: EN "Heavy rains wash loose volcanic ash DOWN mountains" became "Gihugasan sa kusog nga ulan ang luag nga abo sa bulkan PAINGON SA BUKID" = toward/up the mountain. Direction is reversed (should be paubos sa bukid / gikan sa bukid paubos), and the danger of a lahar is precisely that it comes down onto lowland communities. Nothing in the card restores the downhill direction.

fact_en: Lost at night? Look up for the North Star, Polaris! It points to true north to help you navigate back safely.
fact_bis: Na‑lost sa gabii? Pangitaa ang North Star nga si Polaris! Itudlo niya ang tinuod nga north aron makabalik ka nga luwas.

findings.note: title_bis "Polaris Nasala" for "Polaris When Lost". Nasala in Cebuano = was strained/filtered (cf. "pagsala sa sobrang asin" in ffct-35548), or na-sala = committed a fault — not lost, which is nasaag/nawala. The body only says "Na-lost sa gabii?" in English, so no Cebuano word in the card restores the intended meaning.

fact_en:
Does the Moon spin?

Yes! The Moon rotates on its axis, completing one spin in the exact same time it takes to orbit Earth.
fact_bis:
Nag-ikot ba ang Moon?

Oo! Ang Moon nag-ikot sa iyang axis, usa ka beses sa parehas ka oras nga gigugol niya paglibot sa Earth.

findings.note: title_bis "Tuyo Bulan Axis" for "The Moon Does Spin". Tuyo in Cebuano = purpose/intent (Tagalog: dried fish); rotation is tuyok/ikot — the body uses "nag-ikot" correctly. The title reads "Moon's purpose, axis" and never delivers the spin claim the card is about.
